**Proposal**
- I would make the canonical persisted object the thing the indexers already produce, and stop inventing a separate backlog payload type like [chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs).
- The right split is: immutable request payload, mutable backlog state, and runtime-only timing metadata.
- That means the backlog should persist the exact indexed request object from [chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs#L45-L55), while status/execution progress lives beside it instead of being baked into a transformed enum.

**Idiomatic Shape**
- Keep one serializable domain type for “what was requested”.
- Keep a separate serializable state enum for “where it is in processing”.
- Keep `Instant` and other runtime-only fields out of the persisted type.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct IndexedRequest {
    pub id: SignId,
    pub chain: Chain,
    pub indexed_at_unix_seconds: u64,
    pub kind: IndexedRequestKind,
}
```

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum IndexedRequestKind {
    Sign { args: SignArgs },
    SignBidirectional { args: SignArgs, event: SignBidirectionalEvent },
    RespondBidirectional { args: SignArgs, tx: RespondBidirectionalTx },
}
```

**Backlog State**
- The backlog should store `IndexedRequest` unchanged, plus a sidecar state machine:
- `Queued`
- `PendingExecution { tx: BidirectionalTx }`
- `Success`
- `Failed`
- That gives you one immutable request record and one mutable workflow record, which is much cleaner than turning the request itself into multiple storage variants.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum BacklogState {
    Queued,
    PendingExecution { tx: BidirectionalTx },
    Success,
    Failed,
}
```

**Why This Fits Better**
- It removes the current split between `args` and `sign_request_type` in [chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs#L45-L55) plus [chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/mod.rs#L224-L229).
- It removes the need for a backlog-owned request enum in [chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs#L672-L743).
- It preserves exactly one request payload from indexer → stream → protocol → checkpoint → recovery.
- Recovery becomes “deserialize the same request and requeue it”, not “reconstruct the original request by pattern-matching some transformed backlog shape”.

**One Important Refinement**
- I would move `SignBidirectionalEvent` out of [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs#L20-L27) into a domain module like `protocol/request.rs` or `types/request.rs`.
- It is request data, not stream-ops behavior, and backlog/protocol depending on `stream::ops` is a layering smell.

**Runtime Wrapper**
- Since `Instant` is not a persisted domain field, I’d wrap the persisted request when it enters processing:
- `QueuedRequest { indexed: Arc<IndexedRequest>, received_at: Instant }`
- That keeps latency tracking in memory and out of your checkpoint format.

**Net Result**
- Indexers create one canonical request type once.
- The backlog serializes that same request object unchanged.
- Execution progress is tracked separately as workflow state.
- No more `IndexedSignRequest -> BacklogEntry` conversion step.

Yes — if every request kind always has `SignArgs`, it should usually live on the outer struct.

The only reason to keep `SignArgs` inside each `IndexedRequestKind` variant is if you expect one of these to become true:
- some variants do not actually need signing inputs,
- different variants need different signing payload shapes,
- you want the type system to enforce variant-specific fields with no “unused” outer fields.

Given this codebase, [chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/protocol/signature.rs#L45-L55) already shows `args` is common to all requests, and [chain-signatures/node/src/respond_bidirectional.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/respond_bidirectional.rs#L112-L124) also builds `RespondBidirectional` with `SignArgs`. So the more idiomatic model is probably:

```rust
pub struct IndexedRequest {
    pub id: SignId,
    pub chain: Chain,
    pub args: SignArgs,
    pub indexed_at_unix_seconds: u64,
    pub kind: IndexedRequestKind,
}
```

```rust
pub enum IndexedRequestKind {
    Sign,
    SignBidirectional { event: SignBidirectionalEvent },
    RespondBidirectional { tx: RespondBidirectionalTx },
}
```

Why I’d prefer this:
- it encodes the invariant “every indexed request is something to be signed”
- it avoids repeating `args` in every variant
- it keeps `kind` focused on only the extra data that differs by request type

toolCallRounds.response:
Yes — there are still a few good redundancy cuts left, and they’re more structural than cosmetic now.

**High ROI**
- Extract a single `enqueue_indexed_request(...)` helper from [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs#L236-L285). `process_sign_event` and `process_sign_request` do the same three things: record metrics, reject `RespondBidirectional`, insert into backlog, then send `Sign::Request`.
- Collapse the Solana/Hydration request-building logic into a shared builder path. [chain-signatures/node/src/indexer_sol.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/indexer_sol.rs#L196-L282) and [chain-signatures/node/src/indexer_hydration.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/indexer_hydration.rs#L161-L266) repeat the same pattern: validate key version/deposit, derive epsilon, hash payload, build `SignArgs`, then construct `IndexedSignRequest`. A small trait like `ChainSignRequestParts` or a shared `build_sign_request(...)` helper would remove a lot of near-copy logic.
- Move more transition logic into backlog methods. Right now `process_respond_event` and `process_execution_confirmed` in [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs#L325-L526) still know too much about backlog state sequencing. Good next methods would be `backlog.promote_bidirectional(...)` and `backlog.complete_execution(...)` so stream code stops manually coordinating `advance`, `unwatch_execution`, `set_status`, and follow-up request creation.

**Medium ROI**
- Reduce duplicated chain wrapper enums in [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs). `SignBidirectionalEvent`, `RespondBidirectionalEvent`, and `SignatureRespondedEvent` all expose repeated per-chain accessors (`request_id`, `sender`, `source_chain`, `signature`, cloned fields). A trait-based wrapper or macro-generated accessors would trim a lot of repetitive match blocks.
- Unify “respond-follow-up” request creation. `process_execution_confirmed` in [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/ops.rs#L470-L526) and `CompletedTx` in [chain-signatures/node/src/respond_bidirectional.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/respond_bidirectional.rs#L84-L124) already form a clean pipeline, but the stream layer still decides too much. If `CompletedTx` returned a domain enum like `NextRequest`, the stream path would just dispatch it.
- Consider a per-chain backlog state object instead of parallel maps. [chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs#L284-L520) keeps request storage and execution watchers in separate chain-keyed maps. A `ChainBacklog { requests, execution_watchers, processed_block }` would remove repeated `chain` lookups and make transitions more local.

**Lower ROI / Nice-to-have**
- `BacklogEntry` still derives some facts twice: from `execution` and from `request.kind` in [chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/backlog/mod.rs#L702-L745). If you introduced a tiny `BacklogPhase` view/helper, methods like `target_chain`, `typename`, and `is_bidirectional` could share one interpretation path.
- The stream dispatch loop in [chain-signatures/node/src/stream/mod.rs](chain-signatures/node/src/stream/mod.rs#L115-L168) repeats the same `if let Err(err)` logging pattern for every event arm. Not a huge win, but a helper like `log_chain_event_error(chain, "...", future)` would reduce boilerplate.

If I were choosing the next cleanup, I’d do them in this order:
- `enqueue_indexed_request(...)`
- shared Solana/Hydration request builder
- backlog transition helpers for respond/execution flows

If you want, I can implement the first one or two of those now.
